title: Lossy Source Coding with Side Information

items.title: Finite strongly typical sets with support restriction
items.statement: Defines relative empirical typicality for finite laws, including exact exclusion of zero-probability letters and the conditional typical set for a fixed source block.
items.strategy: State the empirical-frequency convention, support rule, and conditional-set notation used by the finite random-coding lemmas.

items.title: Finite type-class cardinality bounds
items.statement: For every attainable type q on a finite alphabet of size m and blocklength n, proves (n+1)^(-m) exp(nH(q)) <= |T_q| <= exp(nH(q)), including zero coordinates.
items.strategy: Use the probability of one type under its own product law, prove that the type q is a mode, and count at most (n+1)^m types.

items.title: Finite random-codebook covering and selected-codeword law
items.statement: For a finite test channel P(U|X), a typical x^n, and an iid P_U codebook with rate above I(X;U), proves the failure probability tends to zero and the first successful codeword has the P_U^n law conditioned on the conditional typical set, uniformly within each conditional type.
items.strategy: Approximate P(U|X) by an attainable conditional type, apply the two-sided type-class bounds, and use the independent-codeword failure product.

items.title: Finite joint-typicality packing bound for independent random bins
items.statement:
Fix $k\ge1$, finite alphabets $\mathcal U_1,\ldots,\mathcal U_k,\mathcal S$, and a joint law $P_{U_1\cdots U_kS}$. Let the source-selection data $Z^n$ and decoder side-information block $S^n$ have any joint law. Independently of $(Z^n,S^n)$, generate mutually independent codebooks whose $M_i$ codewords each have law $P_{U_i}^{\otimes n}$. Generate independent uniform bin labels from $[B_i]$ for every codeword, independently of the source and codebooks. Let the selected true indices $L_i$ be functions of $Z^n$ and codebooks but not the bin labels. In addition, for every nonempty proper $J\subset[k]$, require the complementary selected codewords at indices in $J^c$ to be determined by $Z^n$ and codebooks indexed by $J^c$ alone; this condition is automatic when each terminal selects using its own codebook, and is vacuous for $k=1$. For a fixed positive typicality tolerance, a joint-typicality decoder looks for the unique tuple in the received bins whose codewords and $S^n$ are jointly typical for $P_{U_1\cdots U_kS}$. Suppose there is a common $\eta>0$ such that for every nonempty $J\subseteq[k],$
$$\sum_{i\in J}\frac1n\ln\frac{M_i}{B_i}<\sum_{i\in J}H(U_i)-H(U_J\mid U_{J^c},S)-\eta.$$
Then there is $\epsilon_0>0$ such that, for every fixed typicality tolerance $0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0$, writing $E_n$ for the event that the selected true tuple and $S^n$ are jointly typical, the expected number of wrong jointly typical tuples in its received bins, multiplied by $\mathbf1_{E_n}$, tends to zero as $n\to\infty$. Consequently the probability that $E_n$ holds and a wrong jointly typical tuple exists tends to zero. The case of no side information is represented by a singleton $\mathcal S$.
items.strategy: For each nonempty changed subset, bound the conditional typical-set size by conditional entropy, multiply by product-marginal codeword masses and independent bin-collision probabilities, then sum over the finite subsets.

items.title: Markov typicality for independently selected finite codewords
items.statement: If X,Y,U are finite with U-X-Y and x^n,y^n are sufficiently typical, proves that a codeword selected by the first-match iid marginal-codebook rule is jointly typical with (x^n,y^n), conditional on successful selection.
items.strategy: Condition on each attainable conditional type; uniform assignments within source-symbol classes produce hypergeometric counts whose variances are O(n), and a finite union bound gives joint typicality.

items.title: Finite-alphabet lossy source coding with decoder-only side information
items.statement: Defines the finite IID source model, encoder and decoder maps, normalized bounded distortion, operational rate-distortion function, and its single-letter finite auxiliary test-channel expression.
items.strategy: Specify finite alphabets, the memoryless joint law, the decoder-only side-information interface, natural-log rates, and the finite auxiliary variables U-X-Y and reconstruction map g(Y,U).

items.title: Finite-alphabet multiterminal lossy source code
items.statement: Defines a finite IID k-source, separate deterministic encoders, one common decoder, per-terminal finite bounded additive distortions, rate conventions, and operational achievability.
items.strategy: State each encoder's observation, each reconstruction and distortion criterion, the common decoder, and nats per source symbol.

items.title: Cardinality bound for the finite Wyner-Ziv auxiliary
items.statement: Every finite Wyner-Ziv test channel and reconstruction map can be replaced by one with no larger conditional mutual information, identical source marginal and distortion, and |U| <= |X|+1; consequently the finite single-letter minimum is attained.
items.strategy: Represent each auxiliary value by its posterior on X, its conditional distortion, and H(X|Y,U=u); use a finite linear-dependence perturbation preserving the source law and distortion while not decreasing conditional entropy.

items.title: Convexity, monotonicity, and continuity of finite Wyner-Ziv rate
items.statement: The finite single-letter Wyner-Ziv function is nonincreasing and convex on its feasible distortion interval and continuous at both finite endpoints.
items.strategy: Use nested feasible sets, finite time sharing, compact attainment under the cardinality bound, and endpoint mixtures with a minimum-distortion test channel and a zero-rate decoder-only reconstruction.

items.title: Finite-alphabet Berger-Tung multiterminal lossy inner bound
items.statement: For a finite IID k-source and product test channels P(U_i|X_i), every rate vector satisfying sum_{i in S} R_i >= I(X_S;U_S|U_{S^c}) for every nonempty S, together with finite per-terminal reconstruction maps and distortion constraints, is achievable; this is an inner bound and no general exactness claim is made.
items.strategy: Use independent marginal codebooks, covering at each encoder, the finite selected-codeword Markov lemma, random binning, the all-nonempty-subset packing bound, bounded distortion, and finite deterministic selection.

items.title: Finite-alphabet memoryless Wyner-Ziv theorem
items.statement: For finite alphabets, iid (X,Y), finite bounded distortion d(x,xhat) independent of Y, and side information Y available only at the decoder, the operational rate-distortion function equals min I(X;U|Y) over finite U-X-Y and xhat=g(Y,U), with |U| <= |X|+1 and the expected-distortion constraint.
items.strategy: Prove the converse by finite conditional-mutual-information single-letterization; prove achievability with a typical codebook of rate I(X;U), binning at I(X;U)-I(Y;U)=I(X;U|Y), selected-codeword Markov typicality, packing, bounded distortion, and a diagonal limit.

summary: Prove the exact finite-alphabet memoryless Wyner-Ziv theorem with decoder-only side information and the |U| <= |X|+1 cardinality bound. Distinguish this exact single-encoder region from the finite-alphabet Berger-Tung inner bound, without claiming a general multiterminal lossy region.

title: Lossy Source Coding with Side Information — Examples

items.title: No side information reduces Wyner-Ziv to ordinary rate distortion
items.statement: When Y is constant, verifies that the decoder-only side-information single-letter minimum equals the ordinary finite-alphabet information rate-distortion function.
items.strategy: Compare every auxiliary U and reconstruction g(U) with the induced reproduction channel, then use the admissible choice U=Xhat.

items.title: Lossless Wyner-Ziv endpoint is the Slepian-Wolf rate
items.statement: For finite (X,Y) and Hamming distortion at D=0, computes the Wyner-Ziv expression as H(X|Y), agreeing with the exact one-encoder Slepian-Wolf specialization when the decoder knows Y.
items.strategy: A feasible zero-distortion reconstruction is a deterministic function of (Y,U), so H(X|Y,U)=0; choosing U=X attains H(X|Y).

items.title: Berger-Tung inner bound contains the Slepian-Wolf region
items.statement: With U_i=X_i and Hamming distortion zero, computes the k-source Berger-Tung subset inequalities as the exact Slepian-Wolf inequalities.
items.strategy: Substitute the identity auxiliaries, simplify the conditional mutual informations, and invoke the complete finite-IID Slepian-Wolf theorem for exactness in this lossless special case.

summary: Work the no-side-information and lossless decoder-side-information endpoints, and exhibit the exact Slepian-Wolf special case inside the Berger-Tung inner bound. The general multiterminal lossy region remains explicitly an inner-bound-only statement.
